chapter: Violinists, Jimmy Noon and Decatur Street
title: Playing the parlor and Decatur Street, ending at the Virginia Kitchen
summary: He tells of a poorly paid job at the parlor, playing Decatur Street dives and ending each night at the Virginia Kitchen.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: He was playing with different fellas, you know. Yeah. Around here one time, musicians make the best of the time. Yeah. My father come got me, Frank. Frank come got me one night, knocked on my door. He said, Frank, you got no job tonight. I said, where you playing? He played at the parlor. You know where the parlor park is? No. On the charter right corner from the church. I know, I know.
The parlor park. Near the St. Louis Cathedral?

Yeah, St. Louis, right. I believe it was the first and second door. Yeah. When God drew Frank, he gave me 50 cents. I said, what's this? He said, that's what the job paid $2 for. I said, Frank, don't ever, never, never come here with no 50 cents. I said, what's this? I said, what's this? I said, what's this? I said, what's this? And then we used to play on Decatur Street, Dollar Ballard. We called it the Popeye. You know how the college used to play that? That's how they called it, Popeye. Canuletti. Oh, Little Kay. Little Kay, yeah. He used to play that. Ernie Kay. They call that play. Yeah, call that play. I never played with him. I played close around him. He said, but all around Decatur Street, man, anyway. Then we used to wind up at the last round of, you know what the Virginia Kitchen is on? On Danville between Dolphin and...
Yeah, they had a nightclub day.

Yeah. And that's what we used to wind up every morning. And a gang of us, you know. Playing till daybreak. Each of us a ton, you know. What's this boy's name? He died. He was a saxophone player. He died. He had a brother playing slide and fly and bone. Two brothers. I forgot their name. It's been so long, you know what I mean? Did he stay here or did he go away? No, he was playing here. Well, let's see. Let's see. Do you know what I'm getting here? I'm getting here. I'm getting here. I'm getting here. I'm getting here.
